- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–5% downward bias in next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for smoothing.
